Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I'll follow with a short proposal and attached rate card: 

- Firm rate card: yes — we can provide committed tiers with per-token unit pricing and explicit overage bands.
- Smoothing/rolling window: supported — configurable 30/60/90-day rolling windows to apply soft smoothing before overage billing.
- Burst credits: supported as a one-time cushion tied to onboarding or as an ongoing monthly burst pool for Dedicated customers.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly by default; quarterly true-up available. Credits are applied on the following invoice line.

Subject: internal: Helios pricing posture

Marcus / Ben —

Notes for the Helios appendix: they care about predictability more than the absolute low watermark price. Suggested posture:

- Offer three commit bands with banded per-token pricing and a protective burst cushion equal to 10% of the committed monthly volume for the first 9 months.
- Provide a quarterly true-up (preferred) rather than monthly to reduce churn from transient spikes.
- Include option for annualized Reserved (Dedicated) pool with a 15% baseline discount and configurable burst pool for 10-30% additional uplift at negotiated rate.
- No carry-forward beyond a 90-day smoothing window unless on Dedicated.

If we can show a worked example where their peak month is 2.5x the commit and still only incurs a modest overage with smoothing, they’ll likely accept. I drafted the sample numbers in the spreadsheet.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Commercial proposal (Helios) — commit tiers + sample scenarios

Alicia —

Per our conversation, attached is a Helios-specific commercial appendix (Helios_RFP_Commercial_Appendix.xlsx) and a summarized proposal below. I've included three worked scenarios showing how smoothing and burst cushions affect billed overages.

Summary (proposed):
- Commit Tiers (monthly committed tokens billed at discounted unit price):
  * Bronze: 25M tokens / month @ $0.00030 per token
  * Silver: 100M tokens / month @ $0.00022 per token
  * Gold: 300M tokens / month @ $0.00018 per token

- Overage structure:
  * Overage Band 1 (0–20% over commit): 1.15x base unit price for that band
  * Overage Band 2 (20–100% over commit): 1.5x base unit price
  * >100% over commit: on-demand public rate (no discount)

- Smoothing / True-up:
  * Default: 60-day rolling smoothing window before billing for overages (Helios can choose 30/60/90).
  * Quarterly true-up for invoice reconciliation; monthly billing still issued but adjustments applied at quarter close.

- Burst protections:
  * Onboarding cushion: one-time 15% burst credit applied to first full month post-launch.
  * Ongoing burst pool: optional, pre-purchased monthly cushion (e.g., 10% of commit) that absorbs Band 1 usage.

- Discounts / Dedicated add-on:
  * Dedicated reserved pools: additional 12–18% off committed pricing depending on term (1yr/2yr).

Attached files: Helios_RFP_Commercial_Appendix.xlsx (spreadsheet with 3 scenarios), Redwood-RateCard-v1.pdf

If the structure looks good I can formalize into a small mutual action plan and DocuSign-ready exhibit.

Thanks — happy to walk through the scenarios on a 30-minute call.

Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial
Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia —

Answers inline:

1) Quarterly true-up handling:
   - Monthly invoices will show provisional usage lines (token consumption and provisional overage estimate). Finalized overage charges (net of smoothing and burst cushions) are applied at quarterly true-up and appear as an adjustment line on the first invoice after quarter close. Disputes are handled via our billing disputes process; disputed amounts are flagged and, where appropriate, placed in a 30-day hold until resolved. We provide a reconciliation CSV per invoice and an audit-ready per-token extract for the quarter.

2) Burst pools for Dedicated:
   - Burst pools can be prepaid (recommended for predictable accounting) or configured as a metered pool. Prepaid burst credits are consumed first and appear as a credit line on the invoice. Metered pools are billed at the Band 1 overage rate when consumed. Pricing for prepaid credits is quoted in the appendix (see Tab: BurstPricing).

3) Audit / usage logs:
   - Yes. We deliver a monthly reconciliation CSV and a queryable usage export (per-request: timestamp, route, model, prompt_token_count, completion_token_count, request_id). We can also provide flow logs to your SIEM for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Next steps:
- I've attached Redwood-RateCard-v2.pdf which includes the Dedicated pricing appendices and burst-credit examples.
- I'll draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lists milestones (PO, technical onboarding, go-live, 30/60/90-day smoothing selection) and an exhibit showing the committed tiers and the quarterly true-up language. I'll circulate a DocuSign link for sign-off so Procurement can route it through your CLA workflow.

If you want a quick call to walk through invoice examples, happy to set 30 minutes tomorrow morning PT.

Best,
Marcus Lin
